name: Joseph
charge: Refusing his master’s wife day by day: how can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
summary: Sold by his brothers at seventeen and bought by Potiphar, Joseph was faithful in that which was least, and the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for his sake. Tempted day by day by his master’s wife, he refused, naming adultery a great wickedness and a sin against God long before any law was written at Sinai; when she caught his garment he fled from sin as from a serpent. Lied on and imprisoned, he found the Lord with him in the prison as in the house, and the favour followed him until he stood where he could save the whole house of Israel alive.
offenseFull: The Lord was with Joseph in his captivity, and his master saw that the Lord made everything he did to prosper; Potiphar made him overseer over his house, and the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake (Genesis 39:1-6), the same theme as when Laban was blessed for Jacob’s sake. The Most High deals with his people even in captivity and gives them compassion before those who carried them away captive (1 Kings 8:50). Christ said a man faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much (Luke 16:10). That is the explanation of Joseph: he was a slave, and he was faithful to Potiphar in it, and Potiphar raised him up. The same measure is on us. We are in captivity as he was in captivity, and being in captivity is no licence to steal or lie or rob on the little jobs out here; deal right on them, because the Most High is watching what a man does with the least thing.

His master’s wife cast her eyes on Joseph and told him to lie with her. He refused: no one in the house was greater than he, and his master had kept back nothing from him except her, because she was his wife; how then could he do this great wickedness and sin against God (Genesis 39:7-9). Adultery was known as sin from the beginning, long before Sinai: Abraham kept the commandments, the statutes and the laws, and Abimelech the heathen king knew that one of his people lying lightly with another man’s wife would have brought guiltiness upon them (Genesis 26:5, 10). Note also what he did not say. He did not blame God for being in slavery. The Egyptians did not marry plain women, and she was not hard to look at, and there was no one watching him; and he still said no. She spoke to him day by day, wearing him down, and he would not listen, to lie by her or to be with her; then, on a day when none of the men of the house were within, she caught him by his garment, and he left it in her hand and fled (Genesis 39:10-12). That is the example: flee from sin as from the face of a serpent, for if a man comes too near it, it will bite him, and the teeth of it are as the teeth of a lion (Ecclesiasticus 21:2). He saw sin like a snake and ran like a rabbit; thirty more seconds of entertaining her would have been the bite. He understood the rule his father had taught him: a man who comes to serve the Lord is to prepare his soul for temptation, to take cheerfully whatever is brought upon him and be patient when he is changed to a low estate (Ecclesiasticus 2:1, 4). Jacob was a wealthy man, and Joseph was taken from all of it into a dungeon.
judgmentFull: She lied, and held his garment as evidence, and his master’s wrath was kindled and he put Joseph into the prison without seeking any understanding, for jealousy is the rage of a man, and he will not spare in the day of vengeance nor accept any ransom (Genesis 39:13-20; Proverbs 6:34-35). But the Lord was with Joseph, showed him mercy, and gave him favour with the keeper of the prison, who committed everything in the prison to his hand, and whatever he did the Lord made it to prosper (Genesis 39:21-23). When a man’s ways please the Lord, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him (Proverbs 16:7). Everywhere Joseph went the favour followed, because the Most High was ordering his steps the whole way.

From the dungeon he asked the butler only to make mention of him to Pharaoh, saying he had been stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews and had done nothing there to deserve the pit; and the butler forgot him (Genesis 40:14-15, 23). Before Pharaoh he claimed no interpretation as his own, saying it was not in him and that God would give Pharaoh an answer of peace (Genesis 41:16). He was raised to govern the country that had bought him (Genesis 41:41), and he became the means by which the family that sold him lived through the famine: they thought evil against him, but God meant it for good, to save much people alive (Genesis 50:20). From seventeen he endured slavery, a false accusation and years in the prison without blaming God, and came out where he could save the whole house of Israel alive.

text.text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down thither.
And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
And his master saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.
And he left all that he had in Joseph’s hand; and he knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat. And Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured.

And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee, and all their transgressions wherein they have transgressed against thee, and give them compassion before them who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them:
He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
And it came to pass after these things, that his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.
But he refused, and said unto his master’s wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand;
There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
And Abimelech said, What is this thou hast done unto us? one of the people might lightly have lien with thy wife, and thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us.
And it came to pass, as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her.
And it came to pass about this time, that Joseph went into the house to do his business; and there was none of the men of the house there within.
And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.
Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.
My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.
Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.
And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth,
That she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice:
And it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled, and got him out.
And she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home.
And she spake unto him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me:
And it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled out.
And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spake unto him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his wrath was kindled.
And Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.
For jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
He will not regard any ransom; neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.
But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that were in the prison; and whatsoever they did there, he was the doer of it.
The keeper of the prison looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the Lord was with him, and that which he did, the Lord made it to prosper.
When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.
But think on me when it shall be well with thee, and shew kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:
For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.
Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.
And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.
